extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It is built by converting public video annotations from 11 public video benchmarks into multiple-choice QA pairs to evaluate temporal understanding capabilities of multi-modal large language models.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.citeAs: Li, Kunchang et al. MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. arXiv:2311.17005v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is constructed by selecting videos from 11 existing public video datasets and automatically converting their open-sourced annotations into multiple-choice question-answer pairs guided by 20 temporal task definitions. The authors carefully filter videos for diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty, selecting videos from varied domains and scenes, and primarily choosing intermediate-duration clips ranging from 5s to 35s.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations are collected from 11 public video benchmarks: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filter source data by video diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty. They eliminate short clips with negligible motion and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts, primarily selecting videos from 5s to 35s. For STAR, they randomly shift the start or end points of video clips to increase localization difficulty. For CLEVRER, they exclude questions requiring more than 10 conditions for describing events. They randomly sample 3 to 5 answer options from candidates and shuffle option order. They also use an LLM to ensure answer options have similar and reasonable lengths to avoid answer leakage.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Public video annotations are converted into multiple-choice QA format. For datasets already in QA format, questions may be directly adopted; for others, ChatGPT is used to generate questions based on task definitions. Answer options are constructed either from templates based on ground-truth annotations or generated by ChatGPT for some tasks such as Unexpected Action. The benchmark ultimately contains 200 multiple-choice QA pairs for each temporal understanding task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are automatically generated from existing public video annotations. Guided by temporal task definitions, the authors use ChatGPT to generate questions for videos when needed and construct answer options from ground-truth annotations or via LLM-based generation. The benchmark uses multiple-choice QA rather than open-ended answers to improve evaluation correctness and fairness and to avoid biased scoring by LLMs or manual intervention.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors use multiple-choice QA instead of open-ended QA for evaluation correctness and fairness because open-ended answers would need to be scored by LLMs or user studies, which may introduce evaluation bias or manual intervention. They also process answer options so that lengths are similar and reasonable to prevent answer leakage, and use a prompt design that guarantees 100% option extraction rate.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to evaluate and improve temporal understanding in multi-modal large language models and to pave the path to general video understanding by making models and data publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses avoiding biased scoring of LLMs by using ground-truth video annotations and multiple-choice QA instead of open-ended evaluation. It also notes a minimal source gap between instruction data and MVBench for some tasks, specifically CLEVRER and SthSthV2, meaning evaluation is not strictly out-of-domain for those cases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has a minimal source gap with some instruction-tuning data: CLEVRER in instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference in MVBench, and videos for Action Antonym are from SthSthV2 while antonyms are from PAXION. The paper also notes that some tasks remain difficult for current models, especially position, count, and character tasks, and that visual information alone may be insufficient for some cognition tasks such as egocentric navigation and episodic reasoning, where other modalities like depth and audio could help.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of multi-modal large language models across 20 video understanding tasks. It is presented as a diagnostic benchmark for comprehensive evaluation of open-world temporal understanding rather than for training.
